entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Macrianus Minor was a Roman usurper who played a pivotal role in the Year of the Five Emperors (261 CE) following the death of Emperor Gallienus. He was one of two claimants to the throne, the other being Claudia the Younger.

Macrianus Minor's rebellion began when he and his son Caecilian were appointed as governors of Pannonia and Illyricum by Emperor Gallienus, in an attempt to quell the growing discontent among the Roman military. As their power grew, so did their ambition, leading them to challenge Gallienus' authority.

The conflict between Macrianus Minor and his rival, Claudia the Younger, resulted in a civil war that spanned much of the Eastern Roman Empire. The war was marked by brutal suppression of opposition forces, widespread destruction, and significant loss of life.

Ultimately, Macrianus Minor was defeated at the Battle of Abrittus, where he was killed alongside his son Caecilian. Claudia the Younger emerged victorious, but her reign proved short-lived as she too would meet a tragic end.

Macrianus Minor's rebellion had significant consequences for the Eastern Roman Empire, contributing to its growing instability and paving the way for further civil wars in the decades that followed.

The legacy of Macrianus Minor can be seen in the continued struggle for power within the Roman military and the ongoing impact of his actions on the trajectory of Roman history.
